consumer or person concerned of the allegations of means and ways in
which he is said to have unauthorizedly used electricity, and, should be
given an opportunity of placing his defence. Thereafter the assessing
officer shall record its conclusion with respect to unauthorised use of
electricity, to confer upon himself the jurisdiction to issue provisional
assessment notice. The object of opportunity at the two stages namely,
before arriving at the conclusion of unauthorised use of electricity and
before making final assessment are distinct. In the former, it is the very
220→issue whether the consumer is guilty of unauthorised use of electricity or
not and in later case it is the quantum of amount which he is required to
pay as a compensation and a fiscal preventive measure for committing
such irregularity. The first one is the stage of finding the person guilty and
later one is the stage of determining extent of monetary liability for
compensating electrical undertaking qua the alleged unauthorised use of
electricity by such persons. It is only when the proceedings are conducted
in the above manner, the assessment made can be held valid and not
otherwise.
59. It is true that judicial cognizance can/should be taken of the fact that
230→theft of electricity has become a serious menace and a social evil not only
in the State of U.P. but in the entire country. The electricity has become a
necessity in the present day of society and development of society as well
as nation cannot be conceived of without electricity. The availability of
electricity however is much in deficiency. A huge amount of electricity,
consumed by scrupulous persons is causing a serious loss to public
revenue hampering and obstructing the development of electrical sector in
particular as well as society and nation in general. Therefore, to check
theft of electricity and/or unauthorized use of electricity, stern measures
are required to be taken. The various provisions of Act, 2003 shows that
240→the legislature is also concerned about it and has take several measures
from time to time including making harsh provisions in the statute.
60. However, this by itself would not justify condemnation and
indictment of a citizen or a consumer of electricity by holding him guilty
of unauthorized use of electricity on the vagaries of the officers of
electrical undertaking unless he is disclosed the manner in which he was
found using electricity unauthorizedly on inspection by the officer
concerned and given an opportunity to explain his case, if any. It is well
settled law that no person can be indicted or condemned without giving a
minimal opportunity of hearing. In the case of unauthorized use of
250→electricity found by the assessing officer at any place or the premises etc.
or otherwise, the same has to be disclosed to the person concerned giving
him an opportunity to put his defence. The principles of natural justice

7
WRIC No. - 12783 of 2024
unless excluded by express provision of the Act or by necessary
implication cannot be said to be inapplicable when a citizen or person is
being indicted of a serious charge, i.e., unauthorized use of electricity,
which in some of the cases an offence under Section 135 of Act, 2003.�
260→11.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent nos.2 and 4, on the
other hand, has contended that even if the inspection team did not find
the petitioner abstracting or consuming electricity at the time of
inspection made on 17.12.2022 and theft can be presumed if any
artificial means or means not authorized by the Board or licencee or
supplier, as the case may be, exists for abstraction or consumption or
usage of electricity by the consumer, until contrary is proved that any
abstraction or consumption or usage of electricity has been dishonestly
caused by such consumer, therefore, the action against the petitioner
270→under Section 135 is justified in view of the proviso to sub-section (1) of
Section 135 of the Act of 2003. It is further contended that in view of
sub-section (5) of Section 126 where the period of unauthorized use of
electricity cannot be ascertained, then assessment of usage can be made
for a period of 12 months immediately preceding date of inspection. In
view of the aforesaid, the action under Section 135 of the Act of 2003
and assessment made under Section 126 of the Act stands justified.   
12.
I have considered the submissions of the counsels for the parties
and perused the record. 
280→13.
The relevant questions to be determined by this Court is (1)
whether in view of the inspection report dated 17.12.2022, theft of
electricity as contemplated under Section 135 of the Act of 2003 is made
out against the petitioner and (2) whether the assessment of electricity
usage, by the respondent no.4, is according to the provisions of Section
126 of the Act of 2003 read with clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply
Code, 2005. 
14.
The term �unauthorized use of electricity� as defined under
290→Explanation (b) of Section 126 of the Act of 2003 means the usage of
electricity (i) by artificial means; (ii) by means not authorized by
concerned person or authority or licencee; (iii) through a tempered

8
WRIC No. - 12783 of 2024
meter; (iv) for the purpose other than for which the usage of electricity
was authorized and; (v) for the premises or areas other than those for
which the supply of electricity was authorized. In the case in hand,
unauthorized use of electricity is relatable to usage of electricity by any
300→artificial means. 
15.
The perusal of inspection reports dated 28.10.2022 and
08.12.2022, clearly show that there was no evidence to establish
abstraction or consumption of electricity from the energized line on  the
double pole,  going behind the back of the premises of the petitioner. In
the inspection report prepared on 17.12.2022 by visiting the premises of
the petitioner from inside, an 11KV cable is found lying on the floor. The
conclusion of the inspection team is that with the help of artificial means
unauthorized consumption is possible. There is nothing on record to
310→show that any artificial means was available within the premises of the
petitioner, therefore, the presumption of theft, available with the
inspection team, under proviso of sub-section (1) of Section 135 of the
Act of 2003, is misplaced. 
16.
In the absence of any concrete evidence of abstraction or
consumption of unauthorized use of electricity, the action of respondent
no.4, in presuming the act of theft, is based on no evidence as it would
lead to a situation where any electric cable lying in a premises of a
person can indict him for theft on the ground that if he obtains any
320→artificial means, he could unauthorizedly use electricity, which could
never be the intention of the Act of 2003. In the absence of any positive
act of unauthorized use of electricity resorting to artificial means, which
were found on the spot by the inspection team, no presumption can be
drawn. In view of the aforesaid, the allegation of theft and unauthorized
use of electricity under Section 135 of the Act of 2003 is not found to be
established against the petitioner.
17.
The Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of Ashok
Kumar (supra), has observed that, a huge amount of electricity,
330→consumed by scrupulous persons is causing a serious loss to public

9
WRIC No. - 12783 of 2024
revenue hampering and obstructing the development of electrical sector
in particular as well as society and nation in general. However, this by
itself would not justify condemnation and indictment of a citizen or a
consumer of electricity by holding him guilty of unauthorized use of
electricity on the vagaries of the officers of electrical undertaking unless
he is disclosed the manner in which he was found using electricity
340→unauthorizedly on inspection by the officer concerned and given an
opportunity to explain his case, if any. In view of the aforesaid, in
absence of any positive act of unauthorized use of electricity resorting to
artificial means, which were found on the spot by the inspection team,
no presumption can be drawn that the petitioner was abstracting or
consuming electricity unauthorizedly warranting any penal action.
18.
In view of the fact that the crusher plant of the petitioner had been
directed to be closed down abruptly, under the orders of National Green
Tribunal and the permanent disconnection of electricity had been carried
350→out by the respondent no.4, w.e.f. 12.07.2019, the presence of stone grits
lying in the premises and near the crusher in itself cannot be the basis for
presuming that the crusher plant was being used unauthorizedly by the
petitioner. 
19.
The respondent no.3 while dismissing the appeal of the petitioner
has failed to consider the grounds raised by the petitioner in his appeal.
The observation of respondent no.3 that in the inspection report dated
17.12.2022, it is specifically stated that near the premises of the
petitioner energized 11KV main line is passing by and the jumper is duly
360→connected, is contrary to the report dated 17.12.2022, filed as Annexure-
9 to the writ petition.  
20.
So far as the second issue with regard to assessment of electricity
usage is concerned, in view of the fact that no unauthorized use of
electricity is established against the petitioner, the assessment under
Section 126 of the Act is also unsustainable in the eyes of law. 

10
WRIC No. - 12783 of 2024
370→21.
In view of the aforesaid discussions, the final assessment order
dated 05.07.2023, passed by the respondent no.4, under Section 126 of
the Electricity Act, 2003 and the order of respondent no.3, dated
14.03.2024, dismissing the appeal, cannot be sustained and are hereby
set aside. 
22.
The writ petition stands allowed. No order as to costs.
